_doc: SYSTEM-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): "Something's missing in the core ultra-stable template that's not saying, hey, this is what an ultra-stable system is. This is how ultra-stable runs. This is how ultra-stable bootstraps. This is how ultra-stable becomes autonomous and achieves criticality. The user should never have to provide all of this." This file is that definition, in the template every system is made from. scripts/contract.py --check fails when the code no longer does what it says (every invariant has a probe on this repository's own files, the two ladders equal the code that computes them); scripts/contract.py --write renders doctrine/SYSTEM.md from it, which CLAUDE.md imports, so every agent session in every system starts from it. A system made from the seed inherits all of it; nothing here is supplied by the owner.
what: An Ultrastable system is something that has to keep running and keep improving: a loop it must close, a measure that can be wrong, upkeep that never ends and a running cost its owner accepts (VISION-1). The owner supplies the idea and the budget. The system supplies everything else, server-side, with no person in any loop: it builds, deploys, measures, repairs, improves, promotes and records itself, and it is judged only by what its code does live.
runs: One clock: the Worker's cron runs the tick (worker/src/index.js scheduled, worker/src/tick.js). Every tick reads every metric, files an item for every breach and closes it when the same probe passes, hands work to roles and coding agents, merges, deploys and probes what they return (lane, handoff, sweeper), and records every step in its own database and the hash-chained audit log. GitHub Actions on their built-in token is the second route; a halt (HALT=1) stops every path at once.
bootstrap_stages: read IDEA.md, the founder's one file
refuse a one-off before anything is hired or provisioned (the system test)
write objectives and metrics; every system gets the same liveness set
detect the accounts, credentials and routes that already exist
pick the roles the idea needs, not the whole catalogue
route around each blocker from the case library; at most one owner card per blocker, with a default in effect
write the first backlog, every item with an owner, a trigger and a closing probe
write the organisation's files into the repository
health-check every route before relying on it
create the Worker, its database and its schedule
refuse to finish while any fault of an unattended year has no exercised drill
done only when the deployed Worker answers /health live
ignition_stages: the schema exists and at least one role can take work
the heartbeat completed every step for a streak of ticks and missed no slot
every loop is ticking with good-slot coverage over 24 hours, watched by a second producer
items close with independently verified outcomes and no silent drop
every objective has a probe-backed target: the system is bootstrapped
k_eff = verified deploys / (cost + human touches) stays at or above k_min: autonomy
critical for long enough with 0 open ignition gaps and 0 human touches: criticality
criticality: Ship. Verify. Spend less than it earns. Feed the next loop. k_eff counts only deploys that were verified live; a human touch counts against it. The system computes its own stage from its own tables (worker/src/ignition.js), files the first unmet stage as IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it, and publishes the stage on /health and /live.

invariants.says: It is a system, not a one-off: the bootstrap refuses an idea that fails the system test.
It runs on its own server-side clock; no person, laptop or open session is in any loop.
It proves from minute one that its clock turns, its loops close and its cost and storage stay inside their limits; a breach files its own repair.
It knows how far it is from bootstrap to criticality, from its own evidence, and files what blocks the next stage.
Its success is verified deploys per unit of cost and human touch, measured every tick.
Coding agents only produce pull requests; the server merges, deploys, probes, closes or rolls back.
One halt stops every recurring path; pages keep serving.
Cost is bounded without a hard stop: past the day's allowance it crawls, and what it serves never breaks.
It sets its own goals and turns its own knobs, with a standing goal of a year unattended.
A year unattended is simulated with drills that run the real recovery code, never asserted.
It is not done until the evidence says it is autonomous; its stage is computed, never declared.
It keeps a self-maintained knowledge graph of all its data and proposes new connections.
Its content is produced and refreshed by its own loops; a stale or thin system files its own fix. Static content is not autonomous.
Every visit shows progress from merged changes; a stall dispatches its own repair.
Promotion is part of its role: it serves a guarded social queue and links its siblings.
It is public and discoverable: it describes itself at /.well-known/ultrastable.json and registers in the directory.
It measures its readers with cookieless first-party analytics and acts on what it reads.
Every deploy, handoff and decision is in a hash-chained log; the database stays small by sealing, not forgetting.
Every autonomous decision logs its prediction and is scored against the outcome.
It audits what it does not know and turns gaps into work.
The user does the idea; the system does the backend and speaks in plain words.
It never runs out of improvement work, front end and back end, and keeps a change only when its metric moved.
It pulls every platform improvement and lifts its own general code back to the platform.
Issue inflow never exceeds closures, and every item is inside its SLA.
Every public statement is bound to a probe of what the code does.
No branch outlives its pull request.
It lives in its own repository, made from this template, and the template itself runs no loops.
Every rule and decision lives in this repository as code it consumes; every agent session loads this definition first.
